title: Party crasher JC knows the unaired Dark Skies pilot

as_told.title: JC says he is from Office of Naval Intelligence and offers slow drip disclosure deal

plain: Bryce Zabel is a television writer who co-created Dark Skies, a 1996 TV series about a secret government cover-up of aliens. On the podcast of host Jesse Michels, he says that in 1996 a man crashed a party at his house in Los Angeles. The man introduced himself as JC, congratulated him on the show, and said, "You guys got a lot right." According to Zabel, JC said he had seen the pilot, the show's first episode, which had not yet aired. His writing partner, Brent Friedman, tells the story too on the same episode, and adds more. Brent says JC claimed to be from the Office of Naval Intelligence, the US Navy's spy agency. He says JC offered a deal: they would get access to information, and in return help with a slow drip disclosure program, a gradual release of the truth to the public. If true, it would mean a military agency was trying to use a TV show to prepare the public.
